solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Little French bird in the water

definitions.note: the definition is the French word for little, also used in English for small and dainty

indicators.note: in tells us the bird's letters sit inside the word for water

parts.note: pee is a slang word for urine, i.e. water passed
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small French bird is splashing about in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' is the informal sense, urine, not a pond or sea; 'in' puts the bird inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: French borrowing meaning small, used in English for dainty or slight people and clothes sizes.

clue.text: Gasp coming to huge shows

parts.note: to gasp is to pant for breath
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, used on clothes labels

explanation.surface: Someone gasps on being taken to spectacular performances.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a crossword favourite for 'huge'. A panto is a British Christmas pantomime, a comic family stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomimes, shortened to pantos, are a kind of theatrical entertainment staged in Britain at Christmas.

clue.text: Food had egg in it, as shown by card

indicators.note: in it says the egg is placed inside the word for food

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish, a kind of food
an egg is round, so it stands for the letter O

explanation.surface: A dish containing egg is shown by a card, as at a fortune teller's table.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is the name of a card used in fortune telling packs, and of the pack itself.

clue.text: Lots of vehicles in short road, including very loud one

indicators.note: including says the road word holds the other letters inside it
short says the road word loses its final letter

parts.note: a track is a rough road
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A busy stretch of road is full of vehicles, one of them very noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TRACK to TRAC, which then takes in FF and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is the collective word for the cars and lorries moving along roads.

clue.text: Like a culprit priest in Holy Writ, one to be avoided

indicators.note: in says the priest goes inside the scripture word
to be avoided says the letter for one is dropped from the scripture word

parts.note: Holy Writ is a name for the Bible
the Roman numeral for one is I
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A priest named in scripture as a sinner people should shun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one to be avoided' removes I from BIBLE, leaving BBLE, into which LAMA is put.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the one at fault, so deserving censure or fault-finding.

clue.text: Ointment, alas, ruined old book

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A spoilt ointment, sadly, has wrecked an old volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentations is a book of the Old Testament, traditionally attributed to Jeremiah.

clue.text: Wind from ungenerous Leftie turning up

parts.note: mean means stingy or ungenerous

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up says the word for a leftie reads upwards

parts.note: a red is a left-wing person

explanation.surface: Wind is coming from a stingy socialist who has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is the verb to twist and turn, rhyming with 'find', not air. RED read upwards gives DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to follow a twisting course, just as a river wanders in loops.

clue.text: Left university, say, to get into money making music

indicators.note: to get into says these letters go inside the money word

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
e.g., for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Someone left university to make money making music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is EG, for example. BRASS is northern English slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a style of American country folk music, played on banjo and fiddle.

clue.text: Very happy about wickedness being reduced by 50% in high place

indicators.note: about says the happy word goes round the other piece

parts.note: elated means overjoyed

indicators.note: reduced by 50% keeps only the first half of the wickedness word

parts.note: evil means wickedness

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled that crime has halved in a well-to-do area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by 50%' keeps the first half of the wickedness word; 'about' has the happy word wrap it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something raised up sits at a height, so it is lofty and in a lofty spot.

clue.text: Woman wants bit of love primarily — it's what you'd expect

parts.note: Norma is a woman's name

indicators.note: primarily says the first letter of love is the one taken
bit of together with primarily says only the opening letter of love is used

explanation.surface: A woman wanting a little love is only to be expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and usual things are the ones people anticipate, hence typical and standard.

clue.text: Like childish behaviour that could make mum irate

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the next words can be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A child's behaviour is the sort that would make mum angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish conduct is babyish, showing a lack of grown-up development.

clue.text: Proceed in joint operation and show mutual affection?

definitions.meaning: to work together closely, as two things that accompany each other
lovers walking with fingers clasped; the question mark flags the literal picture

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is figurative, things happening together; the other is literal, a couple holding hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to accompany closely and to walk with palms clasped like sweethearts.

clue.text: No longer having time, admit being away from the urban jungle?

definitions.text: being away from the urban jungle?

parts.note: out of means having run short of, as in out of milk
to own up is to admit, so own means admit

explanation.surface: Short of time, someone confesses to escaping the concrete jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the countryside, away from the city, is being beyond the city limits; 'urban jungle' is a jokey term for the city.

clue.text: Trouble with mother's blind faith

parts.note: to dog is to trouble or plague someone
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A problem with mother's unquestioning belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed accepted without question is a fixed doctrine, which is belief held without proof.

clue.text: Exceptionally able and accurate? Get 'A' in academic qualification

indicators.note: exceptionally says the letters are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: A clever and precise student gets an A grade in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' looks like praise but it shuffles ABLE, ACCURATE and A together.
explanation.definitionFit: The baccalaureate is a school-leaving diploma, such as the French bac or International Baccalaureate.

clue.text: Risky operation with rubbish — the man had to be committed somehow

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risky undertaking
rot means nonsense or rubbish
he is the pronoun for a man
'd is the short form of had, as in he'd

explanation.surface: A gamble gone to waste, and the man had to be sent somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committed' suggests being sent to an institution; here it is promised in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An engaged person is pledged to marry, so committed in one particular way.

clue.text: Do away with a barrier, allowing brother in

indicators.note: allowing, with in, says the barrier lets the brother inside
in completes the instruction to put the brother inside

parts.note: a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: Someone scraps a barrier so as to let a brother in.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or treaty is to repeal or abolish it.

clue.text: Ban pesticides for destroying little things

indicators.note: destroying says the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A call to outlaw pesticides because they kill small creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little things' seems to mean insects, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends, assorted small items or fragments, are what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Decorator has written out an order

indicators.note: written out says the letters of the order are set down in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A painter and decorator has written up an order.
explanation.definitionFit: One who adorns is someone who embellishes or decorates.

clue.text: Copper with shortage of desire, full of hesitation? A type wet inside

definitions.note: a type of cloud, full of water droplets

indicators.note: full of says the hesitation goes inside the other letters

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
um is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: shortage of says the desire word comes up short, losing its last letter

parts.note: lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A policeman lacking drive, full of dithering, a damp sort of fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is the metal's symbol, not a policeman; 'shortage of' drops the last letter of the desire word and 'full of' puts the hesitation in after the C. 'A type' hints at a cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumulus is a variety of puffy cloud, made of water droplets.

clue.text: Very keen to wield the rod

indicators.note: to wield is to brandish and swing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is very eager to use the cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensely enthusiastic is the figurative sense, from something glowing hot.

clue.text: Moulding with two circles enclosing volume

indicators.note: enclosing says the two circles surround the volume

parts.note: each circle looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A moulding design with a pair of rings around a large book.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a rounded convex moulding in architecture.

clue.text: Fancy ornament placed at the back of the small unit

indicators.note: fancy says the letters are elaborately reworked
the back of says only the final letter of the is used

explanation.surface: An elaborate ornament placed at the rear of a small apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unit' looks like a flat; it is a unit of measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanometre is a billionth of a metre, a tiny unit of length.

clue.text: Maybe past being edgy

definitions.meaning: past is one example of a grammatical ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals an example: past, present and future are all grammatical forms of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb form showing time, like past, and an adjective for anxious.

clue.text: A man subsequently detained as someone from foreign capital

indicators.note: detained says the second word is held inside the first pair

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
then means afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: A man is later held as a foreign national.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Athens, the Greek capital, foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Make sudden move as learner occupying seat

indicators.note: occupying says the learner sits inside the seat

parts.note: a bench is a seat
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A learner flinches on taking a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To blench is to flinch or start back suddenly in fear.

clue.text: English lord getting drunk before a party in wealthy location

indicators.note: drunk says the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An English peer gets plastered before going to a party in a rich area.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold, hence any place of great riches.

clue.text: Agree to have some class entertainers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to booking some performers for a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to consent or say yes, a synonym of agreeing.
